records.query: Need the patient's abdominal CT, upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, and serum amylase/lipase plus liver function results, as these are core examinations for confirming or excluding alcohol-related gastrointestinal and pancreatic disease and for differentiating it from cardiac arrhythmia.

Need the patient's electrocardiogram and 24-hour Holter monitoring to exclude alcohol-induced arrhythmia, plus fasting blood glucose and serum ethanol levels to rule out hypoglycemia; these are essential for differentiating the leading hypothesis of alcohol-related GI disease from cardiac and metabolic causes.
records.text:
Image Title: ECG Recording A
Image Description: High-degree atrioventricular block and premature ventricular contractions. ST segments elevated 4-6 mm in leads II, III and aVF, with ST depression in leads V2-V6

Image Title: ECG Recording B
Image Description: Sinus rhythm with short bursts of ventricular tachycardia. Widespread ST-segment elevations (4-15 mm) in leads II, III, aVF, and V2-V6

records.query: Need the patient's abdominal imaging and endoscopic reports, along with serum amylase/lipase and liver function tests, as these are core for confirming or excluding alcohol-related gastrointestinal diseases such as chronic pancreatitis or peptic ulcer, and would clarify the cause of recurrent post-alcohol pain and syncope.

Need the patient's abdominal CT or MRCP to assess pancreatic duct morphology and calcifications, along with fecal elastase and hemoglobin/occult blood tests to confirm chronic pancreatitis or GI bleeding as the cause of syncope; these directly verify or exclude alcohol-related GI disease.

Need the patient's high-sensitivity cardiac troponin and CK-MB levels, plus coronary angiography or echocardiography results, as these are core for confirming alcohol-induced arrhythmia and excluding acute coronary syndrome with myocardial injury; serum ethanol level is also needed to establish alcohol exposure timing.

records.query: Need serum ethanol level and fasting blood glucose to confirm alcohol exposure timing and exclude hypoglycemia, plus 24-hour Holter monitoring and echocardiography results to fully characterize arrhythmia burden and rule out structural heart disease; these are essential for verifying alcohol-induced arrhythmia against remaining alternative causes.

Need the patient's serum ethanol level, fasting blood glucose, 24-hour Holter monitoring, and echocardiography results to confirm alcohol-induced ventricular arrhythmia and exclude hypoglycemia or structural heart disease; these are the core missing evidence for verifying the frontier hypothesis.

Need the actual serum ethanol level and fasting blood glucose results to confirm alcohol exposure timing and exclude hypoglycemia, plus 24-hour Holter monitoring and echocardiography reports to quantify ventricular tachycardia burden and rule out structural heart disease; these are the core missing evidence for verifying alcohol-induced ventricular arrhythmia.

bindings.label: Patient in their 50s presented with recurrent abdominal pain and syncope after drinking alcohol
Symptoms persisted for 2 years and worsened on admission; episodes usually occurred 6-20 hours after alcohol ingestion and lasted 5-10 minutes; syncope occurred only after large alcohol intake
Past medical history included hypertension diagnosed 3 months prior
Social history included smoking and alcohol overconsumption (250g/week) for about 20 years
Alcohol-related GI disease
Alcohol-induced arrhythmia
Alcohol-induced hypoglycemia
Alcohol-related neural disorder
First ECG shows high-grade AV block with premature ventricular beats and extensive ST-segment elevation
Second ECG shows sinus rhythm with short-run ventricular tachycardia and extensive ST-segment elevation
Abdominal CT, endoscopy, serum amylase/lipase, and liver function test results are unavailable
No blood glucose or ethanol level measurements are available
Patient may have acute coronary syndrome with myocardial injury
Troponin level is normal
Coronary angiography shows only 10% stenosis
Serum ethanol, Holter monitoring, and echocardiography results are still pending
Alcohol-induced ventricular arrhythmia
Alcohol-induced coronary vasospasm with secondary ventricular arrhythmia
Alcohol-induced Brugada syndrome
Alcohol-induced high-grade AV block
